newsitem.title: CHILE: CHILE SHARES END FIRM, BOOSTED BY FOREIGN DEMAND.
newsitem.headline: CHILE SHARES END FIRM, BOOSTED BY FOREIGN DEMAND.

text.p: Chilean blue chips closed higher in light trade with the market tracking Wall Street and rising in line with other markets in the region, said traders.
The winning streak is seen continuing at the opening with the bolsa, provided Chilean-issued American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) maintain their upward tilt, they said.
The 40-share index ended unofficially up 0.75 percent at 135.01 points. The general index firmed 0.39 percent to 5,713.98 points.
Turnover slipped to 11.5 billion pesos from 14 billion pesos Tuesday.
"The bolsa was boosted by demand abroad, especially for electricity stocks," said one dealer.
Power generator Endesa rallied 1.57 percent to 324 pesos, while parent company Enersis rose 0.66 percent to 307 pesos.
Traders noted the sector continued to be buoyed by confidence sparked by Endesa Espana's decision last week to buy a controlling stake in Enersis.
Losers included glass-maker Cristales which has tumbled for several sessions following disappointing second quarter earnings, said dealers.
The stock was hit Tuesday by news of ING Barings downgrade to sell from hold, they said.
Cristales ended down 3.65 percent at 2,900 pesos. Other losers included drug producer LabChile, down 1.56 percent at 630 pesos and forestry firm Masisa which shed 0.91 percent to 218 pesos.
